Here's a summary of what I did:\n\n## Summary\n\n**Dependency bump applied** — `pom.xml:236`: `com.h2database:h2` upgraded `2.0.202` → `2.0.206`.\n\n**Root cause of the regression** — H2 renders `TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE` values as strings using a **space** separator and a **variable-length offset** (e.g. `1995-11-02 16:45:04+05:30`, `1995-11-02 16:45:04+00`, `1995-11-02 16:45:04+05`). The old `OffsetDateTimeSerde.deserialize` parsed only strict `DateTimeFormatter.ISO_OFFSET_DATE_TIME`, which requires a `'T'` separator and a fixed offset — so every H2-produced timestamp string threw `DateTimeParseException` → `IllegalArgumentException`.\n\nI confirmed empirically (running both jars against JDBC) that this H2 output format is what flows into the serde and that strict ISO parsing rejects it.\n\n**Fix** — `elide-core/.../converters/OffsetDateTimeSerde.java`: replaced the strict formatter with a `DateTimeFormatterBuilder` that accepts **both** the client ISO format (with `'T'`) **and** H2's format:\n- optional `'T'` or space separator\n- optional seconds and fractional seconds (0–9 digits)\n- offset via `+HH:mm`/`Z` (tolerates `+05`, `+00`, `+05:30`)\n\nSerialization is unchanged (still emits `ISO_OFFSET_DATE_TIME`), and genuinely malformed input (e.g. `2019-06-01T09:42:55.12X3Z`) still throws `IllegalArgumentException`.\n\n**Verification**\n- Existing `OffsetDateTimeTest` (3 tests) pass.\n- Standalone checks against the compiled serde confirm all H2-format and client-ISO strings deserialize correctly, round-trips work, and invalid input is rejected.\n- `mvn checkstyle:check` on elide-core: **0 violations**, BUILD SUCCESS.\n\nNote: local Maven only has JDK 17 while the project's enforcer requires JDK 11; I skipped only the enforcer/JDK-range check locally (compilation targets JDK 11 source level and passed).
